analysisVariables.name: SITEGRy
analysisVariables.label: Pooled Site Group y
analysisVariables.description: Character description of a grouping or pooling of clinical sites for analysis purposes. For example, SITEGR3 is the name of a variable containing site group (pooled site) names, where the grouping has been done according to the third site grouping algorithm, defined in variable metadata; SITEGR3 does not mean the third group of sites.

analysisVariables.name: SITEGRyN
analysisVariables.label: Pooled Site Group y (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of SITEGRy. There must be a one-to-one relationship between SITEGRyN and SITEGRy within a study. \n SITEGRyN cannot be present unless SITEGRy is also present. When SITEGRy and SITEGRyN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

analysisVariables.name: REGIONy
analysisVariables.label: Geographic Region y
analysisVariables.description: Character description of geographical region. For example, REGION1 might have values of "Asia", "Europe", "North America", "Rest of World"; REGION2 might have values of "United States", "Rest of World".

analysisVariables.name: REGIONyN
analysisVariables.label: Geographic Region y (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of REGIONy. Orders REGIONy for analysis and reporting.There must be a one-to-one relationship between REGIONyN and REGIONy within a study. \n REGIONyN cannot be present unless REGIONy is also present. When REGIONy and REGIONyN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

analysisVariables.name: FASFL
analysisVariables.label: Full Analysis Set Population Flag
analysisVariables.description:
These flags identify whether or not the subject is included in the specified population. A minimum of one subject-level population flag variable is required in ADSL. 
 Not all of the indicators listed here need to be included in ADSL. As stated in Section 3.1.4, Flag Variable Conventions, only those indicators corresponding to populations defined in the statistical analysis plan or populations used as a basis for analysis need be included in ADSL. 
 This list of flags is not meant to be all-inclusive. Additional population flags may be added. 
 The values of subject-level population flags cannot be blank. If a flag is used, the corresponding numeric version (*FN, where 0 = No and 1 = Yes) of the population flag can also be included. Please also refer to Section 3.1.4, Flag Variable Conventions.

analysisVariables.name: TRTxxP
analysisVariables.label: Planned Treatment for Period xx
analysisVariables.description: Subject-level identifier that represents the planned treatment for period xx. In a one-period randomized trial, TRT01P would be the treatment to which the subject was randomized. TRTxxP might be derived from the SDTM DM variable ARM. At least TRT01P is required.

analysisVariables.name: TRTxxPN
analysisVariables.label: Planned Treatment for Period xx (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of TRTxxP. There must be a one-to-one relationship between TRTxxPN and TRTxxP within a study. \n TRTxxPN cannot be present unless TRTxxP is also present. When TRTxxP and TRTxxPN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

analysisVariables.name: TRTxxA
analysisVariables.label: Actual Treatment for Period xx
analysisVariables.description: Subject-level identifier that represents the actual treatment for the subject for period xx. Required when actual treatment does not match planned and there is an analysis of the data as treated.

analysisVariables.name: TRTxxAN
analysisVariables.label: Actual Treatment for Period xx (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of TRTxxA. There must be a one-to-one relationship between TRTxxAN and TRTxxA within a study. \n TRTxxAN cannot be present unless TRTxxA is also present. When TRTxxA and TRTxxAN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

analysisVariables.name: TRTSEQP
analysisVariables.label: Planned Sequence of Treatments
analysisVariables.description: Required when there is an analysis based on the sequence of treatments, for example in a crossover design. TRTSEQP is not necessarily equal to ARM, for example if ARM contains elements that are not relevant to analysis of treatments or ARM is not fully descriptive (e.g., "GROUP 1," "GROUP 2"). When analyzing based on the sequence of treatments, TRTSEQP is required even if identical to ARM.

analysisVariables.name: TRTSEQPN
analysisVariables.label: Planned Sequence of Treatments (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of TRTSEQP. There must be a one-to-one relationship between TRTSEQPN and TRTSEQP within a study. \n TRTSEQPN cannot be present unless TRTSEQP is also present. When TRTSEQP and TRTSEQPN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

analysisVariables.name: TRTSEQA
analysisVariables.label: Actual Sequence of Treatments
analysisVariables.description: TRTSEQA is required if a situation occurred in the conduct of the trial where a subject received a sequence of treatments other than what was planned and there is an analysis based on the sequence of treatments.

analysisVariables.name: TRTSEQAN
analysisVariables.label: Actual Sequence of Treatments (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of TRTSEQA. There must be a one-to-one relationship between TRTSEQAN and TRTSEQA within a study. \n TRTSEQAN cannot be present unless TRTSEQA is also present. When TRTSEQA and TRTSEQAN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

analysisVariables.name: TRxxPGy
analysisVariables.label: Planned Pooled Treatment y for Period xx
analysisVariables.description: Planned pooled treatment y for period xx. Useful when planned treatments (TRTxxP) in the specified period xx are pooled together for analysis according to pooling algorithm y. For example when in period 2 the first pooling algorithm dictates that all doses of Drug A (TR02PG1="All doses of Drug A") are pooled together for comparison to all doses of Drug B (TR02PG1="All doses of Drug B"). Each value of TRTxxP is pooled within at most one value of TRxxPGy.

self.title: Planned Pooled Treatment y for Period xx

self.title: Planned Pooled Trt y for Period xx (N)

analysisVariables.name: TRTSDT
analysisVariables.label: Date of First Exposure to Treatment
analysisVariables.description: Date of first exposure to treatment for a subject in a study. TRTSDT and/or TRTSDTM are required if there is an investigational product. Note that TRTSDT is not required to have the same value as the SDTM DM variable RFXSTDTC. While both of these dates reflect the concept of first exposure, the ADaM date may be derived to support the analysis which may not necessarily be the very first date in the SDTM EX domain.

self.title: Date of First Exposure to Treatment

analysisVariables.name: EOSSTT
analysisVariables.label: End of Study Status
analysisVariables.description: The subject's status as of the end of study or data cutoff. Examples: COMPLETED, DISCONTINUED, ONGOING.

analysisVariables.name: EOSDT
analysisVariables.label: End of Study Date
analysisVariables.description: Date subject ended the study - either date of completion or date of discontinuation or data cutoff date for interim analyses.

analysisVariables.name: DCSREAS
analysisVariables.label: Reason for Discontinuation from Study
analysisVariables.description: Reason for subject's discontinuation from study. The source would most likely be the SDTM DS dataset. Null for subjects who completed the study.

analysisVariables.name: DCSREASP
analysisVariables.label: Reason Spec for Discont from Study
analysisVariables.description: Additional detail regarding subject's discontinuation from study (e.g., description of "other").

self.title: Reason Spec for Discont from Study

analysisVariables.name: EOTSTT
analysisVariables.label: End of Treatment Status
analysisVariables.description: The subject's status as of the end of treatment or data cutoff. Examples: COMPLETED, DISCONTINUED, ONGOING.

analysisVariables.name: DCTREAS
analysisVariables.label: Reason for Discontinuation of Treatment
analysisVariables.description: If a subject discontinued treatment in the study, then this variable indicates the reason for discontinuation. This is for discontinuation of treatment in the overall study and not to be used for discontinuation reason within individual treatment periods.

analysisVariables.name: DCTREASP
analysisVariables.label: Reason Specify for Discont of Treatment
analysisVariables.description: Additional detail regarding subject's discontinuation from treatment (e.g., description of "other").

self.title: Reason Specify for Discont of Treatment

analysisVariables.name: EOTxxSTT
analysisVariables.label: End of Treatment Status in Period xx
analysisVariables.description: The subject's treatment status as of the end of period xx, or data cutoff if within period xx. Examples: COMPLETED, DISCONTINUED, ONGOING.

self.title: End of Treatment Status in Period xx

analysisVariables.name: DCTxxRS
analysisVariables.label: Reason for Discont of Treat in Period xx
analysisVariables.description: Reason for discontinuing treatment in period xx.

self.title: Reason for Discont of Treat in Period xx

analysisVariables.name: DCTxxRSP
analysisVariables.label: Reason Spec for Disc of Trt in Period xx
analysisVariables.description: Additional detail regarding subject's discontinuation of treatment in period xx (e.g., description of "other").

self.title: Reason Spec for Disc of Trt in Period xx

analysisVariables.name: EOPxxSTT
analysisVariables.label: End of Period xx Status
analysisVariables.description: The subject's status as of the end of period xx, or data cutoff if within period xx. Examples: COMPLETED, DISCONTINUED, ONGOING.

analysisVariables.name: DCPxxRS
analysisVariables.label: Reason for Discont from Period xx
analysisVariables.description: Reason for discontinuing analysis period xx.

self.title: Reason for Discont from Period xx

analysisVariables.name: DCPxxRSP
analysisVariables.label: Reason Spec for Discont from Period xx
analysisVariables.description: Additional detail regarding subject's discontinuation from period xx (e.g., description of "other").

self.title: Reason Spec for Discont from Period xx

analysisVariables.name: RFICDT
analysisVariables.label: Date of Informed Consent
analysisVariables.description: Date subject gave informed consent. Generally equivalent to DM.RFICDTC.

analysisVariables.name: ENRLDT
analysisVariables.label: Date of Enrollment
analysisVariables.description: Date of subject's enrollment into trial.

analysisVariables.name: RANDDT
analysisVariables.label: Date of Randomization
analysisVariables.description: Required in randomized trials.

analysisVariables.name: RFICyDT
analysisVariables.label: Date of Informed Consent y
analysisVariables.description: This variable may be used in the case where there are multiple consent dates within a study. This date does not need to repeat the date in RFICDT. "y" can start with 1 but it is not required to start with 1.

analysisVariables.name: ENRLyDT
analysisVariables.label: Date of Enrollment y
analysisVariables.description: This variable may be used in the case where there are multiple enrollment dates within a study. This date does not need to repeat the date in ENRLDT. "y" can start with 1 but it is not required to start with 1.

analysisVariables.name: RANDyDT
analysisVariables.label: Date of Randomization y
analysisVariables.description: This variable may be used in the case where there are multiple randomization dates within a study. This date does not need to repeat the date in RANDDT. "y" can start with 1 but it is not required to start with 1.

analysisVariables.name: LSTALVDT
analysisVariables.label: Date Last Known Alive
analysisVariables.description: If this variable is included in ADSL, the best practice is to populate it for everyone. If the derivation for subjects who died differs from the derivation for subjects who are not known to have died, the differences should be noted in metadata.

analysisVariables.name: TRCMP
analysisVariables.label: Treatment Compliance (%)
analysisVariables.description: Overall percent compliance with treatment in the trial. TRCMP may be useful for inclusion in ADSL for reasons such as defining subgroups and/or populations.

analysisVariables.name: TRCMPGy
analysisVariables.label: Treatment Compliance (%) Group y
analysisVariables.description: Grouping "y" of TRCMP, treatment compliance percentage.

analysisVariables.name: TRCMPGyN
analysisVariables.label: Treatment Compliance (%) Group y (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of treatment compliance (%) grouping "y". There must be a one-to-one relationship between TRCMPGyN and TRCMPGy within a study. \n TRCMPGyN cannot be present unless TRCMPGy is also present. When TRCMPGy and TRCMPGyN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

analysisVariables.name: TRxxDURD
analysisVariables.label: Treatment Duration in Period xx (Days)
analysisVariables.description: Treatment duration for period xx as measured in days. More than one of TRxxDURD, TRxxDURM, and TRxxDURY can be populated, but each represents the entire duration in its respective units.

analysisVariables.name: TRxxDURM
analysisVariables.label: Treatment Duration in Period xx (Months)
analysisVariables.description: Treatment duration for period xx, as measure in months. More than one of TRxxDURD, TRxxDURM, and TRxxDURY can be populated, but each represents the entire duration in its respective units.

analysisVariables.name: TRxxDURY
analysisVariables.label: Treatment Duration in Period xx (Years)
analysisVariables.description: Treatment duration for period xx, as measured in years. More than one of TRxxDURD, TRxxDURM, and TRxxDURY can be populated, but each represents the entire duration in its respective units.

analysisVariables.name: TRTDURD
analysisVariables.label: Total Treatment Duration (Days)
analysisVariables.description: Total treatment duration, as measured in days. More than one of TRTDURD, TRTDURM, and TRTDURY can be populated, but each represents the entire duration in its respective units.

analysisVariables.name: TRTDURM
analysisVariables.label: Total Treatment Duration (Months)
analysisVariables.description: Total treatment duration, as measured in months. More than one of TRTDURD, TRTDURM, and TRTDURY can be populated, but each represents the entire duration in its respective units.

analysisVariables.name: TRTDURY
analysisVariables.label: Total Treatment Duration (Years)
analysisVariables.description: Total treatment duration, as measured in years. More than one of TRTDURD, TRTDURM, and TRTDURY can be populated, but each represents the entire duration in its respective units.

analysisVariables.name: DTHDT
analysisVariables.label: Date of Death
analysisVariables.description: Date of subject's death. Derived from DM.DTHDTC.

analysisVariables.name: DTHDTF
analysisVariables.label: Date of Death Imputation Flag
analysisVariables.description: Imputation flag for date of subject's death. If DTHDT was imputed, DTHDTF must be populated and is required. See Section 3.1.3, Date and Time Imputation Flag Variables.

analysisVariables.name: DTHCAUS
analysisVariables.label: Cause of Death
analysisVariables.description: Cause of Death.

analysisVariables.name: DTHCAUSN
analysisVariables.label: Cause of Death (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of cause of death. There must be a one-to-one relationship between DTHCAUSN and DTHCAUS within a study. \n DTHCAUSN cannot be present unless DTHCAUS is also present. When DTHCAUS and DTHCAUSN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

analysisVariables.name: DTHCGRy
analysisVariables.label: Cause of Death Group y
analysisVariables.description: Grouping "y" of DTHCAUS, the subject's cause of death.

analysisVariables.name: DTHCGRyN
analysisVariables.label: Cause of Death Group y (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of grouping "y" of the subject's cause of death. There must be a one-to-one relationship between DTHCGRyN and DTHCGRy within a study. \n DTHCGyN cannot be present unless DTHCGy is also present. When DTHCGy and DTHCGyN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

analysisVariables.name: STRATAR
analysisVariables.label: Strata Used for Randomization
analysisVariables.description: STRATAR contains the combination of values of the individual stratification factors used for randomization. The exact format should be determined by the sponsor. \n This variable is intended for studies that use stratified randomization. \n For example, ">=50, Treatment experienced, N"

analysisVariables.name: STRATARN
analysisVariables.label: Strata Used for Randomization (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of STRATAR. For example, STRATARN=3 when STRATAR=">=50, Treatment experienced, N". There must be a one-to-one relationship between STRATARN and STRATAR within a study. \n STRATARN cannot be present unless STRATAR is also present. When STRATAR and STRATARN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

analysisVariables.name: STRATwD
analysisVariables.label: Description of Stratification Factor w
analysisVariables.description: STRATwD is a full text description of the stratification factor "w". This text description will remain constant for all subjects. These descriptive variables are included to quickly and clearly communicate critical study design information as well as to facilitate integration. \n For example, STRAT3D="Hypertension"

analysisVariables.name: STRATwR
analysisVariables.label: Strat Factor w Value Used for Rand
analysisVariables.description: STRATwR is the subject-level value of the "w'th" stratification factor used for randomization. \n For example, STRAT3R="N"

self.title: Strat Factor w Value Used for Rand

analysisVariables.name: STRATwRN
analysisVariables.label: Strat Factor w Value Used for Rand (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of STRATwR. For example, STRAT3RN=0 when STRAT3R="N". There must be a one-to-one relationship between STRATwRN and STRATwR within a study. \n STRATwRN cannot be present unless STRATwR is also present. When STRATwR and STRATwRN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

self.title: Strat Factor w Value Used for Rand (N)

analysisVariables.name: STRATAV
analysisVariables.label: Strata from Verification Source
analysisVariables.description: STRATAV contains the entire string value represents the combination of values of the individual stratification factors that should have been used and represents the "as verified" value. The STRATAV variables are based on the source documentation and are determined after randomization. If the values used for the randomization of a given subject were all correct, then STRATAV will equal STRATAR. Otherwise, one or more components of the text string for STRATAR and STRATAV will be different. \n The exact format should be determined by the sponsor. \n For example, ">=50, Treatment experienced, Y"

analysisVariables.name: STRATAVN
analysisVariables.label: Strata from Verification Source (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of STRATAV. For example, STRATAVN=4 when STRATVR=">=50, Treatment experienced, Y". There must be a one-to-one relationship between STRATAVN and STRATAV within a study. \n STRATAVN cannot be present unless STRATAV is also present. When STRATAV and STRATAVN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

analysisVariables.name: STRATwV
analysisVariables.label: Strat Factor w Value from Verif Source
analysisVariables.description: STRATwV is the "as verified" subject-level value of the "w'th" stratification factor. If the value based on randomization was correct, then STRATwV will equal STRATwR. \n For example, STRAT3V="Y"

self.title: Strat Factor w Value from Verif Source

analysisVariables.name: STRATwVN
analysisVariables.label: Strat Fact w Val from Verif Source (N)
analysisVariables.description: Numeric representation of STRATwV. For example, STRAT3VN=1 when STRAT3V="Y". There must be a one-to-one relationship between STRATwVN and STRATwV within a study. \n STRATwVN cannot be present unless STRATwV is also present. When STRATwV and STRATwVN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null. \n

self.title: Strat Fact w Val from Verif Source (N)
